correctness.rationale: Variation of constants proves support maximum and nonnegative deficit identity. Exact stationary orientation-resolved edge densities give a positive no-flip coefficient; the total negative occupancy must be O(epsilon), and a bounded Poisson-rate close-pair estimate makes all switched paths O(epsilon^(beta+2)). This forces identical endpoint beta and a strict support speed ceiling. For identical beta, explicit kappa=(v-Rprime)/R and alpha=2(beta+1)v/R yield a time-changed stationary RTP exactly, with smooth positive endpoint matching controls. Moment-system and quadrature checks pass; no infinite conclusions are based on those finite tests.

originality.rationale: The directly motivating 2026 fixed-speed, athermal RTP paper supplies the stationary density and a hierarchy with approximate slow-protocol examples, but its full text does not claim an if-and-only-if finite-time reachability classification, an exactly conserved edge-tail exponent, or the sharp support expansion time. The 2023 RTP shortcut paper has different actuators (time-dependent propulsion velocity), while another 2026 paper uses different active-noise dynamics. Explicit residual risk: a general finite-speed telegraph boundary theorem could imply the no-flip exponent and exact reachable-set criterion without these titles.
residual_risks: Generic finite-speed velocity-jump/transport edge asymptotics or control theory might imply the invariant without matching terminology.

value.rationale: Completes a natural two-actuator reachability question left only approximately handled in the closest direct paper. A robust pathwise edge obstruction supplies a sharp boundary between mathematically possible and impossible full distribution transfers, while an explicit control solves every possible case and a physically interpretable propulsion-limited expansion time separates compression/expansion. This is nontrivial structural information; finite numerics and reproduction of known beta densities are not claimed as its value.
